items.description: Hans J. Wegner’s spacious CH104 sofa for four people fits its distinctive lines, fine comfort and distinguished combination of steel and leather in large, stylish rooms. The sofa is part of the CH100 series that Wegner designed in 1970.

items.description: The KK41180 sofa by Kaare Klint is a compact, two-seater version of a design that was created for the Danish Prime Minister’s office in 1930. With its refined, functionalist form, the sofa is an elegant representation of the designer’s longstanding legacy.

items.name: KK41181 Sofa with high sides
items.description: Kaare Klint designed the KK41181 sofa for the Danish Prime Minister’s office in 1930. With high sides and crossbars beneath the seats, its construction is characteristic of Klint, elegantly combining form and function to make sitting more comfortable.

items.name: OW149-2 Colonial Sofa
items.description: The OW149-2 Colonial Sofa was designed by Ole Wanscher in 1964. Manufactured in very small quantities, the design was virtually unknown until Carl Hansen & Søn launched the entire Colonial Series in 2015.

items.name: OW150 Daybed
items.description: The OW150 daybed by Ole Wanscher is amongst his many designs that have become collector’s items by virtue of their timeless simplicity and beautiful finishes. The distinctive OW150 daybed is ideal for comfort and relaxation in a contemporary setting.
materials: FSC™ Mix-certified oak, oil, TERRA® 20367 Raku

items.description: The TK8 daybed by Thomas Bo Kastholm was designed in 2009 and had the instant makings of an iconic design. Its distinctive shape and sleek finish with carefully-selected materials will enhance any modern setting.

items.name: BM0488L 138x46
items.description: Originally designed in 1958 by Børge Mogensen, Carl Hansen & Søn reintroduces the the versatile Table Bench design, expertly crafted in oak heartwood with cabinetry joints, rounded edges and a double-woven rattan seat. items.name: BM0488S 69x46
items.description: The BM0488S Table Bench is a shorter version of Børge Mogensen’s famous bench with the characteristic woven seat, understated details and precise craftsmanship. items.name: CH004 Nesting Tables
items.description: Hans J. Wegner’s iconic Nesting Tables were first launched in 1952. items.name: CH008 | Coffee Table | Ø78
items.description: The CH008 coffee table was designed by Hans J. Wegner in 1954. The understated and elegant three-legged design has since become one of his most popular pieces.
materials: FSC™ Mix-certified oak, oil, Ø78 cm, H44 cm

items.name: CH011 Coffee Table
items.description: Hans J. Wegner’s CH011 coffee table combines the beautiful and the practical to make an elegant piece of furniture that will naturally fit in many spaces.

items.name: CH106 Coffee Table
items.description: In Hans J. Wegner’s CH106 coffee table, glass and stainless steel are combined in a light and elegant construction. The table is an example that shows Wegner was not limited to designing wooden furniture but also chose steel for his chair and table frames.

items.name: CH108 Coffee Table
items.description: The CH108 glass and steel coffee table is part of Hans J. Wegner’s elegant CH100 series. The brushed flat steel frame has a beautiful, smooth surface which is clearly visible through the sturdy rectangular glass top. The Wegner coffee table is also available in a smaller square version; CH106.

items.name: CH415 Coffee Table
items.description: CH415 was designed by Hans J. Wegner in 1990 as an individual folding table designed for use between his fixed sofa rows at Copenhagen Airport. The Wegner table, with its round top, slim legs and small dimensions, is also very suitable in a home as a small low table which can easily be moved around.
materials: walnut, oil, stainless steel, Ø55 cm, H44 cm

items.name: CH417 | Tray Table | Ø62
items.description: Hans J. Wegner’s CH417 tray table is a clear example of his ability to create functional and, at the same time, beautiful, unique furniture.
materials: laminate, oil, stainless steel, Edge: Oak, Ø62 cm, H33 cm

items.name: KK44860 Sidetable
items.description: Designed in 1932 by Kaare Klint, the minimalist KK44860 Side Table in solid wood displays Klint’s mathematical approach to furniture design, shown through meticulous craft techniques and perfectly measured joints. The square side table is a timeless, elegant design for any modern interior.

items.name: KK66870 Coffee Table
items.description: The KK66870 Coffee Table was designed in 1930 by Kaare Klint. As one of his more decorative designs, this modern round coffee table in solid wood features an elegant, raised band that wraps around the tabletop with a functional shelf below, supported by slightly angled legs.

items.name: ML10097 Ø100
items.description: Mogens Lassen designed the ML10097 Egyptian Table after being inspired by folding stands found in Tutankhamun's tomb in 1922. The table was first shown at the Copenhagen Cabinetmakers' Guild Exhibition in 1940.
materials: oak, oil, Ø100 cm, H54 cm

items.name: OW449 60x60
items.description: Ole Wanscher designed the classic OW449 Colonial Coffee Table in 1964, thereby creating a timeless and harmonious focal point for the entire Colonial Series.

items.name: CH110 Desk
items.description: Hans J. Wegner’s CH110 desk stands out in many ways from his usual style of solid-wood furniture. Created in 1970, it was part of an exclusive office concept. The series features some of Wegner’s most distinctive steel-framed furniture.
materials: oak, oil, stainless steel, 190x95 cm, H71 cm

items.name: PK52 Professor Desk
items.description: The PK52 Professor Desk was designed by Poul Kjærholm for the Royal Danish Academy of Fine Arts. Versatile and slender, the desk established Kjærholm’s reputation for uniting the best of traditional craftsmanship and industrial design.
materials: oak, oil, black powder coated steel

items.name: PK52A Student Desk
items.description: Poul Kjærholm created the PK52A Student Desk by bringing wood and steel together in a clean, light construction. With its pared-down expression the desk is a perfect example of Kjærholm’s great contribution to Danish design.
materials: oak, painted, black  powder coated steel, Black

items.name: BA103 Preludia Dining Table

items.name: BM0698 Asserbo Table

items.name: BM1160 210x82 cm

materials: walnut, oil, brass, 210x82 cm, H72 cm

items.name: CH002 Dining Table
items.description: The CH002 is the smaller of two dining tables that Hans J. Wegner created in 1982. The table expresses Wegner’s functional design philosophy through an appealing solution for modern interiors. The CH002 is crafted to fit smaller spaces, and can be extended easily with two accompanying leaves.

items.name: CH006 Dining Table
items.description: At 90 x 138 cm, the CH006 is a longer version of the CH002 dining table, designed in 1982. materials: FSC™ Mix-certified teak/oak , oil, 190x95 cm, H72 cm

items.description: In 1962 Hans J. Wegner designed the smaller dining table CH337 which, in its basic form, is intended for four people. The table is thus, as a starting point, basically suitable for a smaller family, but could easily be extended. The CH337I insert leaf is sold separately.
materials: FSC™ Mix-certified oak, soap, prepared for 2 leaves

items.name: CH338 Dining Table
items.description: The CH338 Dining Table, designed for 6 people, is a longer version of Hans J. Wegner’s CH337 4-person dining table from 1962. materials: FSC™ Mix-certified oak, oil, 200x115 cm, prepared for 2 leaves, H72 cm

items.name: CH339 Dining Table

materials: FSC™ Mix-certified oak, oil, 240x115 cm, prepared for 2 leaves

items.name: SH900 300x100
